sections.label: SIP extension and end date
sections.summary: The SIP has been extended three times and will end on 28 January 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The SIP has since been extended thrice and will end on 28 January 2026.

sections.label: SIP application and acceptance numbers
sections.summary: As at 31 December 2024, 116 SIP applications were submitted, 77 accepted, and 61 MSCs in severe financial distress assisted.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To give Members some indication of the numbers, as at 31 December 2024, a total of 116 applications for the existing SIP had been submitted and 77 of them were accepted.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Of these, 61 MSCs in severe financial distress were successfully assisted.

sections.label: Streamlining eligibility criteria to one
sections.summary: Clauses 7 and 32 streamline the five criteria to one: total liabilities must not exceed $2 million.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under clauses 7 and 32 of the Bill, which amend sections 72F(2) and 250F(2) of the IRDA, the current list of five criteria will be streamlined to just one, which is the general eligibility requirement that the company's total liabilities must not exceed $2 million.

sections.label: Restructuring Adviser discretion and moratorium
sections.summary: The Restructuring Adviser assesses both SDRP entry requirements, and the company enjoys a 30-day moratorium extendable once up to 30 days.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under clause 6, the Restructuring Adviser has the discretion to assess whether the company meets both the requirements under section 72F(1) for entry into the SDRP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This refers to the general eligibility criteria that the company's total liabilities must not exceed $2 million and that there is no circumstance in existence that would render the company unsuitable for acceptance into the SDRP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: While the company is in the SDRP, the company enjoys a statutory moratorium under the amended section 72K(1) of a period of 30 days, which is extendable once for another period of up to 30 days.

sections.label: Out-of-Court proposal approval by creditors
sections.summary: Clause 16 provides the proposal is approved out-of-Court by creditors at a meeting summoned by the Restructuring Adviser.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Unlike the current programme where the proposal requires Court sanction, clause 16 of the Bill provides that the proposal will be approved out-of-Court and by the company's creditors at a meeting summoned by the Restructuring Adviser under the new section 72M.

sections.label: Two-thirds creditor approval threshold
sections.summary: The proposal is approved by at least two-thirds in value of creditors present and voting at the meeting.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The proposal is approved by a majority of at least two-thirds in value of creditors present and voting at the meeting.

sections.label: Directors' statement on eligibility criterion
sections.summary: Clause 30 allows a company with insufficient or incomplete financial records to submit a Directors' statement to the nominated liquidator that the eligibility criterion has been met.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, clause 30 provides that if the company resolves to enter into the SWUP, but has insufficient or incomplete financial records, the company may submit a Directors' statement to the nominated liquidator that the eligibility criterion has been met.

sections.label: Directors' resolution for winding up
sections.summary: A Directors' resolution can be accepted if the company cannot contact enough members holding a majority in value, cannot obtain a quorum, and has been dormant for three years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In these situations, a Directors' resolution can be accepted as long as the company is satisfied that: despite exercising reasonable diligence, the company is unable to contact enough members who, together, hold a majority in value of its shares for at least three years prior to the date of the Directors' resolution; consequently, the company is unable to obtain the necessary quorum for the extraordinary general meeting to resolve to wind up the company; and finally, the company's operations have been dormant for at least three years prior to the date of the Directors' resolution.

sections.label: SWUP platforms and liquidator switching
sections.summary: Only the Official Receiver's website and Bizfile will publish notices, and clause 42 lets the liquidator switch to other liquidation processes if the company is unsuitable for the SWUP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To reduce the cost of administration, only two platforms will be used in the new SWUP for the publishing of notices, namely, the Official Receiver's website and Bizfile.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 42 provides that the liquidator may switch to other liquidation processes, such as a Court-ordered winding up or a creditors' voluntary liquidation, if the liquidator's assessment is that the company is unsuitable for the SWUP.

sections.label: Reduced eligibility criteria for SIP
sections.summary: The amendment reduces the general eligibility criteria to one $2 million liability threshold, making SIP accessible to more companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The amendment to reduce the general eligibility criteria to just one, which is a $2 million liability threshold, will make SIP accessible to more companies.

sections.label: Safeguards against false declarations
sections.summary: Enforcement measures may not deter bad actors, so the Ministry is urged to strengthen safeguards such as third-party audits or additional documentation, and newspaper notification removal may pose challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While enforcement measures exist to penalise false declarations, these may not adequately deter bad actors seeking to exploit the scheme to expedite winding up processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to strengthen safeguards, such as requiring third-party audits or additional supporting documentation to ensure the integrity of the process. : The removal of the requirement to publish notifications in newspapers may also pose challenges.

sections.label: Reduced grace period for creditors
sections.summary: Reducing the grace period from 90 to 30 days may adversely impact businesses in financial distress, and a 60-day compromise is suggested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Lastly, the proposed reduction of the grace period during which creditors cannot enforce their rights from 90 to 30 days may adversely impact businesses in financial distress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider a compromise, such as a 60-day grace period, to balance the needs of creditors as well as distressed businesses?

sections.label: Moratorium period shortened
sections.summary: Clause 20 shortens the moratorium period from 90 to 30 days.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, clause 20 shortens the moratorium period from 90 to 30 days.

sections.label: SDRP creditor vote threshold
sections.summary: Clause 16 requires only a two-thirds supermajority vote of creditors for SDRP to be approved and binding on all creditors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, clause 16 now requires only a supermajority vote of two-thirds of the creditors for SDRP to be approved and binding for all creditors.

sections.label: SIP application numbers
sections.summary: As at end of October 2024, SIP applications totalled 116, a usage rate of about one in 10 bankruptcies since SIP came into force.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The total number of applications for SIP, as at the end of October 2024, amounted to 116.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given the total number of bankruptcies since SIP came into force, this is a usage rate of about one in 10.

sections.label: Personal bankruptcy applications higher
sections.summary: Personal bankruptcy applications were almost 15,000, an order of magnitude higher, hitting an 18-year high in 2023 and on track to exceed it in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Still, one is left to wonder if we are focusing on meeting a genuine business need with SIP or dancing around other insolvency concerns that may matter more.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is especially relevant when one considers how, over the same period, personal applications for bankruptcy were an order of magnitude higher, amounting to almost 15,000 cases.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Applications hit an 18-year high in 2023 and are on track to significantly exceed that number in 2024.

sections.label: Bankruptcy threshold and debt purgatory
sections.summary: The passage says Singaporeans should not be left in debt purgatory longer than needed and suggests revisiting the $15,000 bankruptcy threshold.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Surely, we do not wish to leave tens of thousands of Singaporeans in debt purgatory for longer than they need to be.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It may also be time to revisit the bankruptcy threshold, which is currently set at a fairly low level of $15,000.

sections.label: Pandemic threshold increases
sections.summary: The threshold was temporarily raised to $60,000 after the pandemic, with the DRS eligibility threshold increased to $250,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notably, the threshold was also temporarily raised in the aftermath of the pandemic to $60,000 and accompanied by an increase in the eligibility threshold for the DRS to $250,000.

sections.label: Insolvency regime for households and firms
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill and urges the Government to consider analogous improvements to the insolvency regime for households as well as firms.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, while I support this Bill, I urge the Government to also consider analogous improvements to the insolvency regime that applies not just to firms, but also for our households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill builds upon the SIP which was introduced in 2021 as a lifeline during the challenging days of the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Bill helps firms including SMEs
sections.summary: The Bill consolidates eligibility criteria, streamlines processes and reduces costs so mechanisms stay accessible to firms of all sizes, including SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By consolidating eligibility criteria, streamlining processes and reducing costs, the Bill ensures that these mechanisms remain accessible to firms of all sizes, including our SMEs, which sends a powerful message that Singapore remains committed to supporting entrepreneurial risk-taking.

sections.label: Survey on business challenges and costs
sections.summary: The survey showed customer demand uncertainty rose from 30% in 2023 to 45% in 2024, and 51% of businesses implemented cost-saving measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The survey revealed that customer demand uncertainty has risen sharply from 30% in 2023 to 45% in 2024, becoming the second top challenge for businesses today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, 51% of businesses have had to implement cost-saving measures to offset rising costs.

sections.label: Amendments for dormant companies to exit
sections.summary: The amendments seek to lower the threshold so these technically alive but dormant and non-operating companies find it easier to exit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Technically alive, but, effectively, dormant and not operating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These amendments seek to lower the threshold for these companies to find it easier to exit.

sections.label: Liability threshold and debt priority
sections.summary: The $2 million liability threshold right-sizes eligible companies, and for SIP 2.0 companies the existing priority of debts in section 203 of the IRDA remains unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The liability threshold of $2 million in many ways acts as a proxy to right-size the kind of companies that can use or benefit from the SIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For all companies eligible for this SIP 2.0, there will be no changes to the existing priority of debts in section 203 of the IRDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The priority scheme amongst creditors, between creditors, will remain unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To summarise, in a winding up, the costs and expenses of liquidation are paid out first, followed by employees' claims for wages or salary.

sections.label: Timeline changed to 30 plus 30
sections.summary: The speaker emphasises that, as stated in the opening speech, the timeline has gone from 90 days to 30 plus 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think all three Members spoke about that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I want to emphasise that, as I said in my opening speech, it has gone from 90 days, to 30 plus 30.

sections.label: Moratorium period and enforcement rights
sections.summary: During the moratorium, rights against the debtor cannot be enforced, moving from a 90-day blanket to 30 days plus a further 30 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Because during the moratorium period, you are not able to enforce any of your rights against the debtor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We felt that this would balance the interests of the parties, moving from a 90-day blanket to a 30-day blanket plus if you need more time, a further 30 days, so 60 days in total.

sections.label: SIP 2.0 eligibility criteria
sections.summary: Eligibility for SIP 2.0 was made simpler and more flexible, shifting from MSC status to owing $2 million or less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First, we made the eligibility criteria for SIP 2.0 simpler and more flexible so that more companies can participate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We moved from defining the eligibility from "Are you an MSC?" – in other words, looking at the identity of the applicant – to "Are you owing $2 million or less?", focusing on the nature of the insolvency at hand.

sections.label: SIP 2.0 for complex companies
sections.summary: Companies with complex ownership or international operations may use SIP 2.0 if the debt circumstances are straightforward and $2 million or under.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: He mentioned a company may have complex ownership structures or international operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But for those companies, if the circumstances surrounding the particular debt is straightforward and it is $2 million or under, then SIP 2.0 could apply.

sections.label: Restructuring Adviser qualifications
sections.summary: Only licensed insolvency practitioners who are chartered or public accountants can be Restructuring Advisers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Only licensed insolvency practitioners who are chartered or public accountants can be Restructuring Advisers.

sections.label: Monitoring and SME education
sections.summary: The Ministry will monitor SIP 2.0 implementation and work with the SME community on its features and downstream assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: One, to Mr Parekh, my Ministry will monitor the implementation of SIP 2.0 and, in due course, to his point about further education, work with the SME community on the features of SIP 2.0 and review how to partner industry stakeholders to provide better assistance downstream, if necessary.

sections.label: Bill strengthens restructuring and insolvency regime
sections.summary: The Bill adds to existing IRDA options for all companies and strengthens Singapore's restructuring and insolvency regime by supporting companies in financial distress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I said, this adds to and does not take away the options that are currently available in the IRDA for all companies – big, small, MSC or otherwise – and whatever is the threshold of the debt for that matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We believe that this Bill strengthens Singapore's restructuring and insolvency regime by giving additional options to support companies through financial distress.

sections.label: Outreach on SIP 2.0
sections.summary: The Government will work with professional bodies, trade associations, organisations and business associations to spread the message, noting SIP 2.0 refines SIP 1.0 and has been socialised with MSCs and business communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Yes, we will work with professional bodies, trade associations, organisations and various business associations to make sure that this is something that is on their radar, in their frame of mind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As you know, there are about 150 to 160 odd insolvency professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will work through these different mediums and forum to get the message across.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But I also want to emphasise that, as I have said, this is a refinement of SIP 1.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have taken what we thought would work, modified it, and now, this is SIP 2.0 about four or five years on from the original SIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, it is something that has already been socialised with the relevant MSCs and business communities.
